transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… mostly other people think I’m doing too much. I don’t really see it that way. There’s just a lot that needs handling—the move, getting the new garage done right, church things, and work. Somebody’s got to keep it all moving.
Have you been feeling unusually high, euphoric, or more irritable than usual lately?

Yeah… I guess more wound up than usual. Like people need to get on board with what I’m trying to do or just get out of my way. One minute I’m joking around, feeling pretty big, and then I’ll snap at my wife or my son over some little question.
Have you been needing less sleep than usual?
I don’t know… maybe a little. I haven’t really been keeping track. I get up and get moving, that’s about all.
Have you been talking a lot more than usual lately?
Maybe. Once I get going explaining what needs doing, I guess I don’t leave much room. My family says I talk over them… too fast for them to even stop me.
Have you been taking on a lot more projects or activities than you usually do lately?

I suppose so. Everybody keeps saying I’m doing too much. But the move won’t handle itself, and the new garage needs to be done right. Then there’s church stuff, and work… somebody’s got to show the younger guys how it’s supposed to be done.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least a couple of weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t put it that way. I’ve had down stretches, sure, but a couple weeks nearly every day… I’m not sure.
Has there been a stretch of several days in a row when you felt noticeably more energized or driven than your usual self?

Yeah… I guess for several days. I just can’t sit in the chair long. After a few minutes I’m up sorting boxes, measuring the garage, loading tools, going back to the old place… feels like my body’s got a motor in it.
Has this wound-up period caused problems for you at work, at home, or with other people?

Yeah… I guess it has. Work pulled me off after something happened with safety. And at home… my wife and the family don’t really trust me with the money or driving, or even decisions about the move right now. They say it got out of hand.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I’m still not sure. I mean, I’ve felt low here and there, but saying it was two weeks, most of the day, nearly every day… I don’t really know.
During this wound-up time, have you had experiences like hearing or seeing things that other people said were not there?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed anything like that.
At any time in your life, have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day?
I don’t really know. I’ve had down spells, sure, but whether it was that long and nearly every day… I can’t say for certain.
Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt depressed nearly every day for two weeks or longer?
I can’t say for sure. I’ve had times I was pretty down, but whether it was nearly every day for two weeks or more… I don’t really know.
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you got unusually wound up like this?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had times where I was more keyed up than usual, but like this… I don’t know. Hard to say.
During this wound-up period, were you ever admitted to a hospital for your mental state?
I’m not sure. I don’t really want to get into all that… I don’t know if I’d call it that.
During this period, were you admitted to a psychiatric hospital?
I… I’m not sure I want to say. I don’t really remember it clearly, and I’d rather not get into that.
During this wound-up period, did you spend at least one night in a psychiatric hospital?
I don’t really know how to answer that. I don’t remember it clearly, and… I’d rather not say more about it.
During this wound-up period, were you unable to do your usual work because of your mental state?

Yeah… I couldn’t really keep working. They pulled me off after something happened at work—safety-wise. And at home, my wife and family… they didn’t want me making decisions about money or driving or the move anymore. It had gotten out of hand.
During this wound-up period, did your family need to take over your usual responsibilities because of how you were acting?

Yeah. My wife and the family pretty much stepped in. They didn’t want me handling money, driving, or making decisions about the move anymore. After I got pulled from work over that safety thing… I guess they felt they had to.
Before this current episode, have you ever had another time in your life when you were unusually wound up like this?
I’m not really sure. Nothing that stands out like this, at least… I don’t think so.
During this wound-up period, did your family need to take over your usual responsibilities because of how you were acting?

Yeah… they did. My wife mostly stepped in, and the family backed her up. They didn’t want me handling money or driving or making decisions about the move anymore. After I got pulled from work for that safety thing, I guess… they just didn’t trust me to manage things.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a current manic episode without psychotic symptoms: elevated/irritable mood, increased energy/activity, pressured/excessive speech, multiple goal-directed projects, and clear functional impairment severe enough to be removed from work and have family take over responsibilities. Psychotic symptoms were denied. Bipolar affective disorder, current manic episode without psychotic symptoms remained a differential, but prior definite manic/hypomanic or depressive episodes were not established, so a single manic episode diagnosis is best supported.
